rationale: As a portfolio, the sheet reads as a small cluster of repeated block/court families with a few threshold variants, not as a broad set of materially distinct three-dimensional spatial types. The dominant language is box-dominated: square block, carved block, lifted block, and stepped block recur across most options. The portfolio does include a few separate readings—voided block, profiled prism, lifted threshold, and stepped/bent tower—but only about six visible families are legible, with one block-derived family occupying roughly half the sheet. That falls short of the required ten materially distinct families and of the 30% dominance cap. The strongest keepers are the most spatially legible and program-fit options: the voided block court, the cut-corner prism, the lifted-threshold mass, and the stepped/bent outlier. The weakest options are those that only tweak the same footprint/roof chassis. The next graph should deliberately expand relation types beyond roof carving into split, bridge, bent-bar, attach-volume, and access-threshold logics while keeping the neighborhood active edge and one usable public void/terrace.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: block-derived courtyard/open-court family with similar square footprint and top void/roof recession; reads as one bar-block lineage despite different edge treatments
block-derived frontage open-court / lifted-threshold family with near-identical footprint logic and similar upper mass containment
profiled/stepped wedge-to-tower family with a cut-corner or lifted threshold gesture and comparable roof emphasis

required_next_relations: Add at least 4-6 new families that are not block/court variants: bent-bar, split-wing, cross-mass, attach-volume, bridge-over-void, punctured slab, or corner-lifted terrace.
Make sure at least one family uses courtyard as a true access relation and not just a roof hole.
Add one or two section-first buildings with a clear ground carve and a calmer upper mass, not just roof sculpting.
Vary footprint logic: elongated bar, L-shape, pinched bar, split mass, offset volumes; avoid repeated square block chassis.
Keep the active west street edge explicit in each new family so the ground threshold is readable as neighborhood frontage.
Preserve a program-specific void/terrace that supports public use, not decorative subtraction, and let upper mass vary without erasing the ground relation.
